Other approaches to this problem include dynamic programming approaches [11], but can take significantly longer to solve. The optimization criteria is the cost of the energy consumed over the entire route. The constraints set to ensure power limits and energy capacities are not exceeded. The cvxopt Python library (an interior point cone programming optimization tool) is used to solve this linear programming problem. In general, a linear programming optimization problem is specified as: minimize 𝒄𝑇𝑥 subject to 𝑮𝑥 ≤ℎ The first step in solving this optimization problem is to pose it in the form above. The x vector represents the power level of each energy source over each interval in the route. It is partitioned into the power provided by either the diesel or fuel cell locomotives and the battery locomotives. It is assumed the consist has either diesel or fuel cell locomotives and not both. The c vector represents a relative cost between the two sources. In our case we chose to make diesel and hydrogen 4 times the cost of the battery power (energy). The primary result of setting these relative costs is it prioritizes using the battery and takes opportunities to charge the battery from the other fuel sources when it makes sense. The more complicated formulation is the constraint captured by the G and h matrices. These two matrices represent the constraints on the power levels in the system, the battery state of charge limits, the total power used for each interval, the maximum power of either the diesel or fuel cells and a minimum power of 0 and the maximum and minimum power of the battery locomotives. The minimum power of the battery is the negative of its maximum power to represent its ability to regenerate energy. The h matrix is partitioned into the five constraints: maximum battery 6 charge, minimum battery charge, power level at each interval, the maximum power level and the minimum power levels for each source. The top part of the G matrix represents the time each power level is delivered over each interval of the route. These become lower triangular matrices in order to integrate the total battery energy over the route during each interval. Thee middle of the G matrix is two identity matrices to represent the sum of power for each interval. Since we want the sum of powers to be greater than or equal, we multiple both sides by -1. The remainder of the G matrix is a 0 and an identity (I) matrix to verify maximum and minimum powers constraints are not violated. The lp solver used in the cvxopt library has an option for “kktsolver” that we set to ‘chol’. This uses a presolve procedure to remove redundant constraints. In general, this lp can result in being infeasible. This can take a significant amount time as it iterates along the constraints in an attempt to find a feasible solution.
